info.name: ScaleSerum — Sales Call Analyzer
info.description:
Ready-made requests for the ScaleSerum Sales Call Analyzer (AI service).

SETUP
1. Set the `apiKey` collection variable (Collection -> Variables tab).
2. `baseUrl` already points at the deployed service.
3. Run the requests IN ORDER - several use ids saved by earlier ones.

ASYNCHRONOUS: every POST /analyze returns an analysis_id immediately. Run the
matching 'poll' request repeatedly until status is completed / failed / skipped.
Transcript-only takes ~20-40s; audio adds transcription time.

Each request has assertions in its Tests tab, so the Postman Runner gives a
pass/fail summary.

Full API contract: SALES_CALL_ANALYZER.md

variable.description: The deployed AI service. For local testing against your own machine, change this to http://127.0.0.1:3001. NOTE: plain HTTP - the API key is sent unencrypted until the service sits behind TLS.
PASTE THE API KEY HERE. Ask the AI service owner for it. Left blank on purpose so a real key is never committed.

Any PUBLICLY REACHABLE audio URL - Deepgram fetches it directly, so localhost or a private bucket will NOT work. The default is a short public sample (one speaker, not a sales call) that proves the transcription path works. Replace it with a real call recording URL - ideally a short-lived signed S3/GCS link - for a meaningful score.
Saved automatically by the POST requests.

request.description:
Confirms the service is up and which subsystems are configured.

EXPECT: sales_call_analyzer.available = true, transcription = "configured",
storage = "configured".

If transcription says not_configured, DEEPGRAM_API_KEY is missing from .env.
If storage says not_configured, MONGODB_URI is missing — every /api/sales-calls
request will return 503.

The key itself is never in this response.

exec: console.warn('DEEPGRAM_API_KEY not set — audio requests will report transcription_not_configured');

request.description: Every /api/* endpoint is gated by the X-API-Key header.

The fastest end-to-end check: no audio, so Deepgram is skipped entirely and only Gemini is called.

EXPECT: 200 with status "queued" and an analysis_id. This is NOT the report —
run request 3 to poll for it.

The analysis_id and call_id are saved into collection variables automatically.

Poll every ~5 seconds until status is completed (about 20-40 seconds).

WHILE RUNNING: status is queued / analyzing / scoring, and scores is null.
WHEN DONE: the full report.

CHECK BY EYE:
- scores.overall_100 is a number, scores.band is null (thresholds are not configured)
- scores.weighting = "equal_unweighted_placeholder" (no business weights set)
- transcript.speakers: speaker_0 = sales_rep, speaker_1 = customer
- analysis_quality.degraded = true and warnings include no_timestamps
  (a pasted transcript has no timings, so tone criteria are not applicable)
- every criterion with a rating carries evidence with verified: true
- call.disposition_source = "rep_reported" — the AI never replaces your CRM outcome

exec: console.log('Still running:', b.status, '— send this request again in a few seconds.');
pm.test('scores are null while running', () => pm.expect(b.scores).to.be.null);
pm.test('no timings on a pasted transcript', () => pm.expect(b.transcript.timestamps_available).to.be.false);

item.name: 4. Idempotency — resubmit the same call costs nothing

request.description:
Byte-for-byte the same body as request 2, with the same call_id.

EXPECT: idempotent_hit = true and the SAME analysis_id. No second Gemini call,
no second charge. This is what protects you from a double-click in the CRM.

Run this only AFTER request 3 shows completed.

IMPORTANT: `audioUrl` must be reachable by Deepgram over the public internet.
A localhost path or a private bucket URL will fail with audio_unreachable.

The default is a short public sample. It is ONE speaker and is NOT a sales call,
so expect a low score and many not-applicable criteria — that is correct
behaviour, and it proves the transcription and diarization path works.

For a meaningful score, replace `audioUrl` with a real two-party call recording
(a signed URL from your storage is ideal).

Poll until completed. Watch status go transcribing -> analyzing -> scoring.

CHECK BY EYE:
- transcript.source = "deepgram", timestamps_available = true
- transcript.segments have real start/end seconds — this is what lets the UI jump
  the audio player to the moment behind a score
- transcript.speakers shows the diarized speakers; roles stay "unknown" unless
  someone is identifiable from the conversation
- processing.transcription_ms and audio_seconds_submitted are populated

With the default single-speaker sample you should also see the warning
"single_speaker_detected" — the system reports it rather than pretending.

exec: pm.test('no fabricated scores on failure', () => pm.expect(b.scores).to.be.null);

item.name: 7. Failure — no audio and no transcript

request.description:
Nothing to analyse.

EXPECT: HTTP 200 (not 422) with status "failed" and reason
"no_audio_or_transcript". Nothing is spent — neither Deepgram nor Gemini is
called. This matches the always-200 contract used across this API: the backend
gets a stable reason code instead of an exception.

exec: pm.test('failed with a stated reason', () => pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('failed'));

request.description:
Submit, then poll the returned analysis_id.

EXPECT eventually: status "failed" with a transcription reason, and
scores: null. A failed analysis NEVER produces a neutral scorecard — a sales
manager cannot tell an invented evaluation from a real one, so we do not make
one.

This takes ~15-30s because the provider error is retried with backoff.

exec: console.log('Poll request 3 with this id to see the failure:', b.analysis_id);

request.description:
The most recent analysis for a call — for a backend that kept the call_id but
not the analysis_id.

EXPECT: the same report as request 3. An unknown call_id returns 404.

Recomputes the scores from the STORED RATINGS under the current framework
configuration. No Deepgram call, no Gemini call, no cost.

Run it as-is and the score will not change — nothing has been reconfigured.

TO SEE IT WORK: edit sales_call_analyzer/sales_framework.json, set
"rating_scale" to { "absent": 0.0, "weak": 0.2, "adequate": 0.5, "strong": 1.0 },
bump "framework_version" to "sales_v2", restart the server, then run this again.
The score moves and rating_scale_mode becomes "configured" — which is exactly how
management's weights get applied to calls that were already analysed.

Requires analysisId to point at a COMPLETED analysis (run 2 and 3 first);
otherwise you get 409.

exec: console.log('409 is correct if that analysis is not completed — run requests 2 and 3 first.');

request.description:
A four-party conference call, sent as a STRUCTURED transcript — note that
Deepgram is skipped entirely, because a structured transcript already contains
what it would produce.

Poll with request 3 (the analysis_id is saved automatically).

CHECK: speaker_0 is sales_rep (they introduce themselves), but NOBODY is marked
customer — nobody identified themselves as Meera, so speakers 1, 2 and 3 stay
"participant" with name: null. The system declines to guess rather than putting
a wrong name in front of a manager.

exec: console.log('Poll with request 3 — expect 4 speakers, no customer role assigned.');
